tier_reason: The README 'How fast is it?' section pastes first-party CLI output: on a MacBook Pro M1 Pro (2022-12-30) LAME 3.100 reports 88.773x play/CPU and shineenc reports 318.0x realtime, plus outdated Raspberry Pi runs (LAME 3.99.5 1.8216x, Shine 3.6x). There is no benchmark script, no compiler or flags for either binary, and single runs, so it stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README, first-party, MacBook Pro M1 Pro (arm64), 2022-12-30: LAME 3.100 at 128 kbps qval=3 reports 88.773x realtime (play/CPU; zsh time 3.609 s total) and Shine 318.0x realtime on a 5:18 stereo 44.1 kHz WAV, about 3.6x faster (derived from page data). The 318.0x is 318 s divided by a whole-second timer reading of 1 s (shineenc uses time()), so the true Shine time could be anywhere under 2 s and the ratio is only bounded below at about 1.8x (derived from page data). Outdated Raspberry Pi run (model not named): LAME 3.99.5 1.8216x (3:06) vs Shine 3.6x (1:35) on a 5:39 file, about 2.0x (derived from page data). Nexus 5: Shine 24.2x realtime, no LAME number.
corrections.baseline: LAME 3.100 (M1 Pro run) and LAME 3.99.5 (outdated Raspberry Pi run) CLI, 128 kbps CBR, qval=3, joint stereo with psychoacoustic model
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated for either README run. The repo's Makefile.am builds libshine/shineenc with -O2 -funroll-loops -fno-exceptions -Wall -fsigned-char (compiler not named); the LAME build is a stock 'LAME 3.100 64bits' binary of unknown origin.
corrections.hardware: MacBook Pro arm64 M1 Pro (current numbers); Raspberry Pi with model not named and Google Nexus 5 (Shine only) in the outdated section
corrections.stars_or_usage: 422 stars, 77 forks; github.com/savonet/shine resolves to toots/shine; used as FFmpeg's libshine encoder (issues #22, #28) and by Liquidsoap
corrections.caveats: Speed is bought with lower quality: Shine has no psychoacoustic model (README 'Limitations' says so and calls the algorithm 'rather simple'), encodes plain stereo, while LAME runs its full psychoacoustic model at qval=3 with joint stereo, so the ratio compares different amounts of work at the same bitrate. No quality measurement exists anywhere in the repo (issue #27 'Quality comparison' open since 2017 with no reply). Single runs from pasted CLI output; shineenc's realtime figure uses whole-second time() resolution (src/bin/main.c), so 318.0x means 'finished within about 1 s' and is imprecise. LAME's figure is CPU-time based, Shine's is wall-clock. The two M1 runs used differently named input files (/tmp/decoded.wav, /tmp/bla.wav) of the same length. Open correctness issues: #24 full-amplitude sine input produces distorted output, #37 final frame may be truncated, #39 padding bit wrong at 32 kHz/48 kbps from float truncation in layer3.c; none touches the timing itself. A third-party ARM NAS anecdote on forum.serviio.org (Shine 42 s vs LAME 6:09 on a 3:48 file, '13x faster', little gain on x86) is search-snippet only. README says the code is Gabriel Bouvigne's late-1990s encoder via Pete Everett's fixed-point RISC OS port; issue #25 asks why it is LGPL when the original Shine seemed GPL. Last commit 2023-01-01, more than three years ago.

notes: Numbers match the README exactly; tier C confirmed. Key extra finding: shineenc times with time() at 1 s resolution, so the 318.0x and the derived 3.6x are coarse (true ratio at least about 1.8x); the quality trade-off is unmeasured. COPYING is the GNU Library GPL v2 text with no per-file headers or version clause, so '-only' is not stated anywhere (left uncorrected); forum.serviio.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED.
